thread:
Support: FYI — ACME submitted a feature request via support ticket #5421: they want a per-route cost + latency breakdown in Console. They need it for Q3 finance review.

Ana: Thanks. Can we get the exact use-case? Are they looking at live per-request cost or daily aggregates?

Support: Key ask pasted from ticket: 'show cost by API route, group by model and env, with 7/30/90 day windows; ability to drill to examples that drove the spikes'. They asked for export to CSV and permission controls.

Mike: Sounds like a mix of analytics + example tracebacks. Core questions: do we compute cost server-side (recommended) or estimate client-side? Also, cost attribution to routes needs token counting per request + model pricing table.

Sophie: We already bake token counts in our logs, but the 'route' concept is product-defined (people use different route ids). We need mapping from request metadata -> route id. Does ACME use a header or path?

Support: ACME uses a header x-app-route set by their gateway. They can add it if needed.

Jordan: Proposed triage: make this P1 for Dedicated/Enterprise customers only, P2 for hosted. ACME is an enterprise pilot with a reserved instance — they pay monthly.

Ana: Agreed to prioritize but let's scope MVP tightly. MVP should include: daily aggregates (cost, median latency, p95 latency) by route+model+env, CSV export, basic RBAC check to hide cost for non-admins, and drill to a sampled list of request ids with timestamps. No live streaming of per-request costs initially.

Mike: Acceptance criteria suggestion: 
1) UI: new 'Cost by Route' dashboard in Console showing table + trend lines for 7/30/90d.
2) Backend: nightly job that computes route/day/model aggregates and stores in metrics store.
3) Drill link resolves to trace view with up to 100 sampled requests and a direct link to Request Inspector.
4) CSV export returns same rows as UI.
5) RBAC enforced via existing Console permissions.

Sophie: Data availability note: our current logs have token_count per request but we don't persist model_price at request time (pricing can change). For accuracy we should compute cost at time-of-query using a pricing snapshot applied during aggregation. Need small schema change to store pricing_snapshot_id with aggregates.

Jordan: Timeline ask from ACME: wants preview by 2024-07-20 and GA by 2024-08-15. That feels tight.

Ana: Realistic timeline: 3 sprints (6 weeks) to MVP if we reuse existing metrics infra + minimal UI. Otherwise 9 weeks. We should commit to a preview for 2024-07-22 if engineering agrees to a focused scope.

Mike: Engineering constraints: we need one backend owner (I'll take it) and one frontend (Sophie if ok). Need infra help for nightly job and storage — @ConsoleBot can you allocate a metrics slot?

ConsoleBot: metrics-queue allocated: job-slot-42. ETA provisioning: 2 business days. :white_check_mark:

Sophie: I can take frontend work. My concerns: table perf for orgs with 100k routes. For MVP we'll limit to top N by cost and add pagination.

Ana: Scope negotiation with ACME: propose MVP scope above, offer a follow-up phase for live per-request streaming and full route-list support. Ask ACME to accept preview date and confirm they can add x-app-route header.

Support: ACME responded in ticket: they can add header and are willing to be in preview. They also asked for role-based CSV shares to their finance team.

Jordan: Add a small enhancement: CSV export endpoint should support an email-delivery option for large exports (async job). Mark as P1 for enterprise.

Mike: Risks: price changes -> historical inconsistency, sampling bias in drill requests, and data freshness for finance deadlines. Mitigations: store pricing_snapshot with aggregate, include sample size in drill UI, and ensure nightly job runs before business hours.

Ana: Owner assignments: Mike (backend, cost calc + pricing snapshot), Sophie (frontend + UX), Jordan (release + infra coordination), Support (customer comms + validation), Ana (PM + acceptance).

Sophie: UX note: table columns: route, model, env, total_cost, avg_latency, p95_latency, requests, sample_link. Add a small sparkline for trend.

Mike: API sketch for aggregation endpoint (for the backend/frontend discussion):
```
GET /api/orgs/{org_id}/costs/routes?start=2024-06-01&end=2024-06-30&group_by=route,model,env
Response: [{route_id, model, env, date, requests, tokens, total_cost, median_latency, p95_latency, pricing_snapshot_id}]
```

Ana: Launch criteria (GA): beta customer signoff (ACME + 1 other), automated test coverage for cost calc, RBAC checks, CSV export validated, less than 2% discrepancy between nightly aggregate and sampled live calc in test corpus.

Jordan: Communication: plan a short preview demo with ACME on 2024-07-25, include finance team, get feedback on columns and export.

Support: I'll draft email to ACME with MVP scope, preview date 7/25, and ask them to confirm header rollout.

Ana: Next steps checklist:
- Mike: start backend PR for aggregation job (due 2024-06-28)
- Sophie: mockups + prototype (due 2024-06-30)
- Jordan: infra provisioning + CSV async job (due 2024-06-27)
- Support: customer comms draft (tomorrow)
- Ana: update roadmap & add ticket to product board (today)

Mike: noted. Will open JIRA epic and link to ticket #5421.

Sophie: will post mockups in #design once ready.

Ana: Thanks all. If no objections, we'll lock MVP scope and commit those dates. :thumbsup:

Support: No objections from ACME so far. They want the CSV delivered to finance emails.

Jordan: I'll add a small privacy note to the export: only include request ids and timestamps if the org opts in; otherwise redact example text.

Ana: Good catch. Let's keep PHI safety first.

ConsoleBot: Reminder: automatic changelog entry will be generated when PRs are merged.

Mike: Closing loop — will post PR link here when opened.

Sophie: Will post mockup link.

Support: I'll update ticket and mark as "in design" once mockups are up.

Ana: End of thread — moving to product board.
